response: Multiple SNP testing in BRCA2 and BRCA1 female carriers can be used to improve risk prediction models when combined with clinical and demographic markers. Although random survival forests did not yield higher performance compared to Cox proportional hazards, the addition of a genetic SNP score to clinical assessment has shown improvement in prediction performance. This suggests that incorporating multiple SNP testing into clinical assessment may enhance the accuracy of risk prediction models for BRCA2 and BRCA1 female carriers, and warrants further investigation to fully explore its potential.
